title: Restore NMI card display metadata after approved payments (0.5.3)
description:
## Problem and release boundary
IdentityPro staging QA on 2026-09-07: Billing and renewal shows Payment method: — after approved paid-trial payments for four accounts. All four have active subscriptions and active saved methods with vault references, but card_brand/card_last4/card_exp_month/card_exp_year are NULL on both approved attempts and methods. This establishes missing display metadata, not renewal failure.

Investigated v0.5.2 at 9f30107eaf13f4a84fa4a1aaa04299246fedcc09 on investigate/nmi-card-display-0.5.2. Target integration/0.5.3 was created directly from that tag. Do not merge current master or release its unreleased features/schema v5. Schema v4 already has the necessary columns; no schema change is expected.

## Live evidence
Read-only staging DB inspection plus exact NMI transaction queries confirmed:
- Dalton / 12526739722: Visa ending 1111.
- Donald / 12526745436: Mastercard ending 1111.
- Donna / 12526750752: Discover ending 0009.
- Thomas / 12526751572: JCB ending 2595.
All four provider query responses contain expiry as well. Local display fields remain NULL. No provider mutation or DB update was performed. Original sale bodies are unavailable: whether missing last-four data was omitted by NMI or rejected during parsing remains unproven. Do not weaken full-PAN rejection to guess at this cause.

## Confirmed parser defects and executable reproduction
crates/syrup-rail-nmi-client/src/client/response/form.rs:88-107 accepts cctype/card_type but ignores cc_type and always sets expiry to None. response/xml.rs:239-260 accepts cc_type and masked cc_number but also always sets expiry to None. client/text.rs already has parse_expiry, used by the JSON parser.

Temporary unit probes against the unchanged v0.5.2 implementation ran with cargo test -p syrup-rail-nmi-client --lib qa_053_probe -- --nocapture. Result: 3 expected failures, 1 passing control. The temporary tests were removed. These were synthetic provider fixtures, not captured sale responses.
- Classic fixture: response=1&response_code=100&transactionid=txn_probe&customer_vault_id=vault_probe&cc_type=Visa&cc_number=4xxxxxxxxxxx1111&cc_exp=1029. Approval remains Approved, but brand is None instead of Visa and expiry is (None,None) instead of (10,2029): two failing probes.
- XML fixture: <nm_response><transaction><transaction_id>txn_probe</transaction_id><condition>pendingsettlement</condition><cc_type>Visa</cc_type><cc_number>4xxxxxxxxxxx1111</cc_number><cc_exp>1029</cc_exp></transaction></nm_response>. Expiry is (None,None): third failing probe.
- Control passes: both formats extract last4=1111 from masked cc_number and XML extracts Visa. A parser-only fix does not explain or remediate the entire staging symptom.

## Confirmed flow gap
- crates/syrup-rail-nmi/src/adapter.rs:67 maps the sale response directly; syrup-rail-postgres/src/enrollment_application/initial.rs:189 applies it immediately.
- syrup-rail-postgres/src/enrollment_application.rs:1327 upserts the method directly from the response descriptor, including NULL values.
- Exact reconciliation candidates in syrup-rail-postgres/src/reconciliation.rs:153 exclude approved attempts. Lifecycle reconciliation updates settlement/reversal fields, not method display details.
- Reapplying an approved initial attempt in enrollment_application/initial/approval.rs:55 returns before upsert_payment_method. Approval replay is not a metadata backfill API.
- billing_portal.rs reads local method descriptors only. IdentityPro renders — when cardLastFour is absent.

## Fix scope
A. Correct classic cc_type alias handling and parse cc_exp in classic and XML responses. Retain conflicting/duplicate-field handling, safe last-four parsing, canonical brand display, redaction, and existing payment-outcome authority.
B. Provide bounded read-only-provider metadata retrieval and persistence for approved saved methods with incomplete descriptors, usable for new approvals and explicit repair of existing rows. Keep NMI protocol handling in the NMI client/adapter and canonical writes in syrup-rail-postgres. Design an additive entrypoint as needed; hosts must not edit canonical tables directly. Fetch outside transactions; revalidate exact account/scope/subscriber/transaction and still-current method identity under existing locks before storing safe descriptors. Missing/conflicting evidence must not erase existing good data. Preserve immutable charge evidence, payment status, access, vault reference, amounts, and renewal schedule. Never replay a sale or re-apply financial approval to refresh metadata. Query failure must leave approval intact and permit a later bounded retry. Late refresh after replacement/deletion/scrubbing must not restore stale or scrubbed data.

## Host follow-up and exclusions
IdentityPro consumes the patch, invokes the supported refresh path, and backfills its four records. Host scheduling and UI wording remain host-owned. Blank hosted-field validation and generic duplicate-failure messaging are separate IdentityPro issues; do not change NMI duplicate protection. Investigation is complete; implementation/release remain open.

## References
https://docs.nmi.com/reference/query (cc_type, masked cc_number, cc_exp)
https://www.postman.com/nmi-integration-support/nmi-public-documentation/documentation/if9qbqu/payment-api (official NMI Payment API examples)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Regression tests cover classic cc_type, classic/XML cc_exp, existing aliases, invalid/conflicting descriptors, and unchanged payment decisions.
2. Approval with empty descriptors followed by an exact provider query populates the billing portal; existing approved methods use the same supported refresh path.
3. Missing metadata, query timeout, malformed/conflicting evidence, and repeated refresh never cause another sale, change financial history/access, or erase good descriptors.
4. Tests prove exact ownership/correlation and replacement/scrub race safety; no provider I/O occurs inside transaction locks.
5. Shipped schema-v4 artifacts stay byte-identical to v0.5.2; no unreleased master code is included; relevant tests and required repo gates pass before closure. IdentityPro staging retest is separate from synthetic-fixture evidence.

title: Preserve financial replay compatibility across metadata parser upgrades
description:
Full-branch review round 3 of integration/0.5.3 found an upgrade compatibility regression. Source: native Codex; independently reproduced by the parent. Reviewed HEAD: 1af44d1767b04a5fb0192c257f894ee8ee46c1af, base v0.5.2: 9f30107eaf13f4a84fa4a1aaa04299246fedcc09.

The NMI XML parser now adds cc_exp to the normalized ProcessorEvidence. A v0.5.2 approved observation parked after an application/event failure has NULL expiry even when that XML contained expiry. The same observation parsed after upgrade has populated expiry. processor_charges/storage.rs::matching_charge compares every immutable evidence field with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, including expiry. Reconciliation forwards the new observation through approval application and fallback parking; every attempt can fail with "processor charge replay evidence changed". The new metadata refresh requires an already approved attempt and cannot recover this unapplied approval.

Master comparison: master@6fccde09c2dd21bb914a82c11b591c4b6d4f9506 still uses the strict expiry comparison. Its enrollment outcome pipeline forwards the observed evidence; it does not substitute the retained charge evidence. This is not an existing master fix to backport.

Reproduction on canonical schema v4: temporary enrollment test qa053_expiry_upgrade_probe uses application_fixture with fail_event=true. It parks an approved outcome whose expiry is absent (the old parser's normalized shape), confirms review_required and NULL immutable expiry, then disables event failure. Applying the otherwise-identical outcome with expiry through apply_reconciled_subscription_enrollment_gateway_outcome fails with the exact immutable-evidence error. Replaying the retained outcome succeeds and creates the subscription. The probe passed (1 test, 6.76 seconds). This is a synthetic normalized-evidence reproduction, not a captured provider-response integration test. The old/new XML parsing difference is separately visible in the parser diff and existing parser tests.

Release policy: user explicitly requires 0.5.3 to remain compatible and directs breaking changes to Beads for 0.6.0. Do not weaken immutable financial replay equality, migrate financial evidence, or require a coordinated host cutover within this patch loop. A redesign of the financial evidence/replay contract belongs to the 0.6.0 workstream. Merely logging this issue does not make the current 0.5.3 parser changes safe to ship: before release, either establish a compatible solution or narrow/defer the parser enrichment. The README instruction to retain normalized evidence is not enough to repair the built-in fresh-query reconciliation path.

Acceptance: retain existing financial identity/decision/conflict guarantees; prove old persisted evidence survives identical provider observations parsed after upgrade across supported payment workflows; preserve immutable charge evidence; distinguish display enrichment from financial authority. Include a regression with parked approval and a retained-evidence control. Keep any breaking contract/schema/cutover work off integration/0.5.3.

title: [R-41] Give the Jig installer lock an owner and generation
description:
Audit ID: R-41
Authoritative subsystem: INFRA-02
Final rank: 29 of 32
Disposition: recommend
Impact: Removes an ABA race that can permit concurrent install-root mutation and corrupt or destabilize the shared tool installation.
Confidence: high
Estimated effort: medium
Blast radius: medium/generated

## Evidence
- scripts/install-jig.sh:157-161 uses an empty lock directory, 30s wait, fixed 300s stale threshold
- scripts/install-jig.sh:292-303 removes a lock solely by mtime age
- scripts/install-jig.sh:318-330 has no owner/generation/heartbeat
- scripts/install-jig.sh:333-336 unconditional EXIT cleanup removes the path currently at the lock name
- scripts/install-jig.sh:339-355,370-390 holds the lock across cargo install
- scripts/jig:150-162 routes concurrent commands through shared install roots
- .agent/jig-managed-paths.json:19-20 marks installer upstream-template-owned

## Current Complexity
A live install over 300 seconds can have its lock stolen; the old process's trap can then delete the replacement lock (ABA), allowing concurrent writers to one Cargo install root.

## Proposed Representation
Absent | Held { owner_pid, acquisition_id }; atomic mkdir plus owner record, reclaim only a provably dead owner, release only a matching acquisition ID, fail closed on uncertain liveness.

## Smallest Credible Scope
Upstream installer template/rendered snapshot, then regenerate scripts/install-jig.sh; launcher/profile/install-root interfaces unchanged.

## Regression Risk and Migration
Medium: portable PID liveness, reuse, permissions and legacy empty-lock recovery need conservative behavior; retain bounded diagnostics.

## Dependencies and Sequencing
- upstream Jig template change and managed regeneration

## Audit Notes
Coordinator independently verified every cited local line on 2026-08-22.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Keep one Jig cargo install alive for more than 300 seconds.
2. Start a second installer and let it remove the first process's age-stale lock directory and acquire a replacement.
3. Let the first process exit and observe its unconditional trap can remove the replacement lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fake-cargo concurrency harness: live >300s remains exclusive, killed owner reclaim, old exit cannot remove replacement, profile-root reuse unchanged.

description:
Canonical explicit-skip, rejection, duplicate, and supersession record for the 2026-08-22 simplification audit.

Completed subsystem skips
- FRONT-01 — Frontend applications: No tracked frontend source and frontend_apps is empty.
- CORE-01 — Validated identity, money, and resolution primitives: Closed wire enums already have exhaustive mappings and round-trip tests; a registry/macro would hide policy or replace direct matching with scans.
- CORE-05 — Foreground subscription command and outcome models: Renaming/moving the already-generic four-operation payment result is public churn without improving representation. Shared redaction is already context-owned; three small operation-specific Debug projections are explicit security policy, not material duplication.
- CORE-06 — Renewal dispatch and failure policy model: Renewal model already uses closed enums/locked terms; public long constructor is a compatibility wrapper already superseded internally; SQL repetition is required for query pushdown; no material local simplification.
- CORE-10 — Customer billing read model and raw-card screening: Portal DTOs intentionally permit partial display data; exact-plan inputs are nominal boundaries; PAN scanner is cohesive/security-sensitive and no measured benefit supports a streaming rewrite.
- CORE-11 — Core public facade and package contract: The long explicit root facade is a deliberate public-API curation gate consumed broadly; examples are already minimal external-consumer contracts and package fields/dependencies have active uses. Wildcards/modules/include machinery would weaken stability or add ownership.
- CLIENT-01 — Raw NMI client construction, credentials, errors, and report admission: Two short Classic response sequences do not justify a helper that merely relocates branching.
- CLIENT-04 — Raw-client internal test harness and standalone packaging: After extracting facade/public-contract ownership to CLIENT-05, the internal transport/fixture/identity test harness and standalone package check are appropriately implementation-specific. Request-budget refactoring was below materiality and no further simplification cleared the threshold.
- NMI-01 — NMI gateway operation adapter: The adapter’s only material signal was the duplicated mutation-reference recognizer; after verification it is owned authoritatively by NMI-03/reference.rs. Adapter outcome mapping, private Result<(),()> validation and provider-bounded straight-line transforms are already cohesive.
- PG-01 — Versioned PostgreSQL schema and runtime conformance contract: Complete versioned artifacts and fresh/upgrade duplication are intentional compatibility evidence; v3 nullable state tuples are constrained relational shapes; splitting attempt subtypes or introducing PostgreSQL enums/descriptors would add joins/migration rigidity or hypothetical indirection without removing current complexity.
- PG-02 — SQLx generated metadata and offline gate: SQLx metadata is generated; the gate already has a closed PrepareMode and explicit install/prepare/cleanup phases; release-tag discovery deliberately avoids a second schema manifest. Replacing three schema-v3 literals would require a build script/symlink/dependency and worsen ownership.
- PG-03 — Gateway-account metadata and host transaction/error bridges: Explicit nominal host error wrappers already share a redacted source and exhaustive regression coverage; generation would hide security-sensitive Display policy.
- PG-07 — Provider-free subscriber mutations: Cancellation intentionally owns a host/outbox transaction while claim/clear own provider-free local transactions and grants remain caller-transaction capabilities. A generic dispatcher or async transaction helper would hide distinct error/rollback/authority semantics for only two similar shells.
- PG-11 — Grant, cancellation, deletion, and scrub operations: Its grant-state candidate was assigned to CORE-03, and both lock-policy findings were reassigned to the existing authoritative helpers in PG-05 and PG-04. The remaining grant/cancellation/deletion code has no separate material simplification.
- PG-12 — Entitlement projection and protected-write guard: Pending/admitted transaction types intentionally gate commit authority; lock-before-clock ordering and wide one-snapshot projection are security/concurrency semantics. Candidate enum/query/typestate rewrites would hide or duplicate behavior.
- PG-13 — Billing portal persistence projection: First/continuation pages already use a closed private query enum and plan-specific SQL; portal shares a repeatable-read entitlement snapshot and selects a narrow privacy-safe projection backed by a matching partial index. Candidate DTO/fragment/cursor changes were stylistic or weakened corruption/plan behavior.
- PG-17 — Host integration and transactional outbox example: The example’s repeated split event kind/semantic kind/payload and raw-then-typed replay checks are intentional versioned-wire evidence; host transaction and helper surface are compiled instructional ownership, not production abstraction debt.
- PG-19 — PostgreSQL public facade and package contract: The private module map and explicit flat re-exports are enforced public-API policy with primary and transaction-local consumer tiers; feature gating/package metadata are deliberate release contracts. Nested modules, wildcard/macro exports or service-only pruning would add compatibility surface or break supported paths.
- INFRA-01 — Workspace metadata, general CI, and security baseline: After extracting release, advisory, and public-API ownership, workspace metadata and general CI already use explicit manifests/jobs with intentionally distinct permissions, tools, caches, and isolation; Cargo.lock duplication is generated resolution, and no structural simplification cleared materiality.
- INFRA-04 — Dependency advisory policy: The wrapper already encodes one closed absent/unreachable/reachable RSA policy, constructs one positional argument vector, invokes cargo-audit once, and has dedicated coverage for all three states plus audit failure. Removing the local flag is line-count-only; extracting CI adds indirection.
- INFRA-05 — Public API and documentation contract: The gate has four explicit facade paths and three small direct checks, inline regression probes, rustdoc and doctest composition, and accurate narrow-policy documentation. An AST helper or shared crate registry would add tooling/coupling without removing material state or branching.

Rejected or demoted candidates
- Make outbound request budget valid by construction (CLIENT-01): Correct and low-risk but below materiality: private callers already use the checked constructor, the zero Default state is never observed, and the change mainly removes impossible Result plumbing.
- Enumize TransactionQuery (CLIENT-02): Both selectors may validly coexist and must each be response-bound; a three-variant enum would only relocate the shape.
- Map/Cow form values or unified form/JSON transport (CLIENT-02): Borrowed secret ownership, ordered duplicate-capable protocol fields and distinct certainty semantics are intentional.
- Map-based lossless JSON or unified decoder abstraction (CLIENT-03): Ordering/duplicate evidence and protocol-specific absence/malformed/nesting rules are intentional.
- Generic raw-HTTP fixture/harness builders (CLIENT-04): Specialized test servers express distinct reset, retry, and concurrency lifecycles; abstraction would hide wire evidence.
- Independent adapter-owned mutation-reference recommendation (NMI-01): Superseded duplicate of R-19; exact grammar ownership belongs to NMI-03/reference.rs, with adapter.rs only a dependent call site.
- Shared current-schema selector (PG-02): include_str! requires a compile-time path and the standalone gate intentionally cannot depend on the query-owning crate; abstraction would relocate three obvious literals into a more fragile mechanism.
- Rename stale CI job label from schema v1 to v3 (INFRA-01): Valid presentation drift noted for infrastructure review, but not itself a material structural simplification.
- SchemaVersionContract descriptor (PG-01): Production entrypoints already close over fixed version/columns/fingerprint constants; no drift evidence makes the descriptor hypothetical.
- Payment-attempt subtype tables or generated schema templates (PG-01): Would add joins, migration and source-of-truth surfaces while shipped artifacts must remain immutable and complete.
- Local gateway identity snapshot consolidation (PG-06): Superseded by authoritative CORE-07 whole-gateway-identity finding R-10; PG-06 is only an affected consumer.
- Generic local transaction helper for claim/clear (PG-07): Two sites only; lifetime/boxed-closure machinery would preserve rather than remove phase-specific error and rollback semantics.
- HostChargeTargetStore trait split (PG-08): Transition-only consumers exist, but the public published trait and documented single-store host implementation would need compatibility adapters that outweigh current benefit.

- Grant revocation nullable fields (PG-11): Superseded by authoritative CORE-03 R-03.
- Service reconciliation reconstruction dispatch (PG-14): Superseded by PG-05 R-26.
- CLIENT-05 duplicate public-test finding — superseded by R-15: Fresh CLIENT-05 review independently found the same black-box test boundary already recorded from CLIENT-04; retained one authoritative finding under CLIENT-05.
- R-04 (CORE-01) — rejected after materiality/over-abstraction audit: Closed wire enums already have exhaustive mappings and round-trip tests; a registry/macro would hide policy or replace direct matching with scans.
- R-05 (CORE-05) — rejected after materiality/over-abstraction audit: Renaming/moving the already-generic four-operation payment result is public churn without improving representation.
- R-06 (CORE-05) — rejected after materiality/over-abstraction audit: Shared redaction is already context-owned; three small operation-specific Debug projections are explicit security policy, not material duplication.
- R-07 (CORE-04) — rejected after materiality/over-abstraction audit: The aggregate constructor already rejects the claimed invalid state/timestamp combinations; making the inner public constructor fallible mostly relocates validation and creates compatibility churn.

title: Plan financial evidence normalization evolution for 0.6.0
description:

The display-only observation boundary introduced for 0.5.3 should remain separate.

This is a deferred design task, not a dependency of the metadata bugfix release. Produce a concrete proposal only when a financial normalization change is needed. Compare preserving existing normalization with versioned evidence profiles, identify any required forward-only migration and host rollout, and prove old retained approvals and queued reconciliation survive the upgrade.
